How to read the figures

33.8kg74.5lb
The manufacturer states a figure with a unit.
0
The manufacturer states the value zero. That is a measured number, not an empty field.
yes
The manufacturer states that the robot has this.
no
The manufacturer states that the robot does not have this.
not stated
The manufacturer states nothing about this field.
visible in a photo only
The information can be seen in the manufacturer’s photo but is written nowhere.
14kgA30.9lbA
The letter in the grey square after a figure points to the source the figure came from. Robots with several sources carry several letters.
1,100mmB43.3inB
A dashed letter marks a secondary source – a datasheet, manual or developer documentation from the manufacturer, or a press report used only where the manufacturer gives no figure.
Payload, walking
A stroke before a field name means the figure carries a caveat that affects how it compares with other robots. The caveat is printed with the figure.

The four states

Stair step and payload each exist in two variants. Only compare fields with the same label.

We do not resell any robot on this site, and we take no payment from the manufacturers.

Every figure in the catalogue has a source and a retrieval date. If the manufacturer does not state it, the field becomes not stated — it never becomes an estimate.
